FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.

2. When practising Interactive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Listening.

3. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. porte
   B. livre
   C. fenêtre
   D. chaise

4. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.

   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.

7. When practising Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

8. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.

10. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good morning / hello
   B. Thank you
   C. Excuse me
   D. Good night only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Reading Expression markings Narrative flow Pronunciation Articulation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
